reason: The reading stands: re-opened packet.js veda 84 --verse 8.39.4 (revision 275528, 2020-09-29): Sāyaṇa glosses śam as śāntinimittam and yoḥ as viṣayayogajanitam qualifying mayaḥ sukham, and closes yaḥ kaścanāpi devo yadi hūyate agnir eva sarvaṃ karoti; Wilson’s note names the first as Sāyaṇa’s; evidence re-found verbatim; verse.js and entry-check ok. The plain sense does not stand as written. (1) Tone: every verse of 8.39 ends on the refrain that all the others die away (Wilson, following Sāyaṇa: may all our adversaries perish); ‘wishing all the others away’ softens a wish for their death into a wish for their absence, against rule 6 (state it in one plain clause, no softening). (2) Plain: the text calls Agni ‘the worshipper’s blissful messenger’ (8.39.3) and ‘our envoy’ (8.39.9), going on his embassy between both gathering-places (8.39.1); ‘the gods’ messenger’ is not the text’s phrase and reads as sent by the gods. Also minor drift: viṣayayogajanitam is born of contact with the objects of sense, not of the objects themselves. The replacement in better passes entry-check (43 words).
better: A hymn to Agni, every verse wishing that all the others die away, calls him the worshipper’s messenger; Sāyaṇa, on 8.39.4, reads the delight as happiness born of calm and of sense contact, and takes Agni as doing all, whatever god is called.
